extracted.intended_audience: research community, prospective and current NIDDK/NIH grant applicants, institutional stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional report describing NIDDK funding outcomes, policies, and metrics (FY1997–FY2020 focus with FY2020 emphasis), including paylines, investigator demographics, funding mechanisms, and trends for R01/R37 and training awards. Intended to document progress toward NIDDK guiding principles and to provide data to the research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining a vigorous investigator-initiated R01 research portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and prioritize a strong investigator-initiated R01/R37 research portfolio as a core guiding principle of NIDDK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDDK commits a majority of Research Project Grant funding to R01/R37 awards (81% in FY2020). The report documents number of R01/R37 awards, expenditures, median costs, and trends over time to demonstrate support for this principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting pivotal clinical studies and trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Support clinical research involving human subjects (HS+) as a strategic funding priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and report the proportion of extramural funding and R01/R37 funding supporting HS+ research (e.g., ~40% of all extramural funding and ~36% of R01/R37 in FY2020). Uses Kotchen et al. (JAMA) definition of HS+ for coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting a steady and diverse pool of talented new investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize support for new investigators, including Early Stage Investigators (ESIs) and New-Not-ESI, to maintain pipeline and investigator renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDDK applies differential paylines for ESIs (higher payline) and tracks numbers of ESI applications, unique ESIs applying, and ESIs awarded; monitors ESI share of applications and awards and changes in payline over time as part of this commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fostering exceptional research training and mentoring opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustain and monitor funding for training and career development awards (F, K, T mechanisms) as part of commitment to workforce development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percent of extramural budget for F/K/T awards, number of awards by type and activity code (e.g., K01, K23, K99), trends in award counts, and T32 slots. Note decisions affecting specific programs (e.g., ceasing K24 new awards after 2018).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual generation and posting of application and funding trend data
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce and publish data and analyses of application and funding trends annually to inform the research community and demonstrate commitment to guiding principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDDK committed (since May 2012 Advisory Council presentation) to generating additional data on application and funding trends and posting updated data on the NIDDK website annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data scope and exclusions for trend charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and document exclusions: charts exclude initiatives (RFAs), ARRA funds, and Special Statutory Funding Program for Type 1 Diabetes awards except where noted (Figure 8 includes initiative data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except where explicitly stated, figures/tables exclude RFAs and ARRA; Figure 8 is an exception. This scope affects interpretation of trend data and comparisons across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-horizon selection for figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose appropriate fiscal year ranges for figures to provide context (most charts use past 10 FYs; some extend to FY1997 to show pre-doubling era; ESI figures start FY2010).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expanded time horizons where helpful to illustrate effects of major historical events (e.g., NIH budget doubling 1998–2003) and to contextualize post-doubling trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payline policy and adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK adheres closely to established paylines but exercises limited programmatic discretion to fund programmatically important applications beyond the general payline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In FY2020 general payline was the 16th percentile for established investigators and 25th percentile for ESIs. NIDDK may include a limited number of programmatically important applications beyond the payline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stricter payline for large-budget R01 applications
rubrics_metrics.description: R01 applications requesting $500,000 or more in direct costs are subject to additional programmatic scrutiny and a stricter payline (10th percentile in FY2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-budget applications have a tighter funding threshold and extra program review to manage portfolio resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile binning and inclusion criteria for funding-curve analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Place R01 applications into percentile bins (1–5 covers 0.1–5.0, 6–10 covers 5.1–10.0, etc.) and include only applications scoring at the 50th percentile or better in certain analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only R01 applications scoring 50th percentile or better are included in the Figure 2 analysis; unscored applications, scored apps with no percentiles, and those scoring above the 50th percentile are not reflected and were not funded in FY2020. This affects the shape of funding curves and percent-funded calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of unscored / no-percentile / >50th applications exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly note that unscored applications, scored applications with no percentiles, and applications scoring above the 50th percentile are excluded from specified charts and were not funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting figures (e.g., Figure 1), understand that excluded applications (n=1,378 in FY2020) are not shown and were not funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and categorization of investigator status (Established, New-ESI, New-Not ESI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize PIs as Established Investigators, Early Stage Investigators (ESI / New-ESI), or New-Not ESI with explicit criteria for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established Investigator = received substantial NIH support disqualifying them for New/ESI status ≥1 year prior; ESI = first R01 recipient in FY, completed terminal degree or clinical training within past 10 years and not previously competed successfully for substantial NIH independent award; New-Not ESI = first R01 recipient who is a new investigator but does not qualify as ESI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track number of competing R01 applications (including resubmissions) over time and by application type
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor counts of competing R01 applications received by fiscal year, distinguishing new vs renewal and including resubmissions where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures show trends from FY1997–2020 and highlight changes such as increases in new applications and decreases in renewals; use these counts to assess applicant behavior and policy impacts (e.g., end of A2 submissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Track funded R01/R37 grants (competing and non-competing) and award composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Count and analyze numbers of new, renewal, and non-competing R01/R37 awards issued by fiscal year to understand portfolio size and composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures document increases during NIH doubling, declines in some periods, and rebounds post-2016; use to assess support levels over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track total expenditures on R01/R37 awards (includes Direct + Facilities & Administrative costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report total dollars spent on R01/R37 grants per fiscal year, including both direct and F&A costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 6 shows total expenditures increased from $383.5M (FY1997) to $1,053.5M (FY2020); interpret increases as resulting from more awards and rising median award costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track median total cost per R01/R37 award
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor median award total costs (direct + F&A) for R01/R37 awards by fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Median cost reached $448,049 in FY2020; rising median costs contribute to overall expenditure growth and inform budgetary planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio breakdown by funding mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize extramural funding by mechanism (RPGs, SBIR/STTR, Research Centers, Research Careers, Training, Other Research, Contracts/IAAs) and report percentage distribution over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 8 shows majority of extramural research funding is RPGs; define each mechanism and include which activity codes belong in each category to enable consistent classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project Grants (RPGs) activity-code distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Within RPGs, track distribution by activity code (R01, R21, R37, P01, U01, Other R, Other U) and report percent distribution over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 8A and accompanying definitions clarify what is included in 'Other R' and 'Other U' and allow assessment of relative emphasis on R01 vs other RPG mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and report number of investigators supported by at least one R01/R37
rubrics_metrics.description: Count PIs supported by at least one R01/R37 in each fiscal year and break down by investigator category (New-ESI, New-Not ESI, Established).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 9 reports average counts (e.g., ~1,800 established PIs, ~66 ESIs, ~68 New-Not ESIs annually over 11 years) and uses these to assess stability of investigator pool and match of new investigator addition to departure of senior investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track growth and impact of Multiple Principal Investigator (MPI) awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure number and percent share of MPI R01 awards over time and assess contribution to number of PIs supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 10 shows MPI awards grew from 6% (FY2011) to 22% (FY2020); increase in MPI awards likely contributed to stabilization/increase in number of PIs supported despite other portfolio changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI-specific application and award metrics and success-rate calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor number of ESI R01 applications, unique ESIs applying, number of ESIs awarded, and calculate ESI success rate as percentage of unique ESIs who applied and were funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 11 shows trends in ESI applications and awards; success rate shown above ESI awarded bars and is used to judge effectiveness of differential paylines for ESIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of ESI applications and awards relative to all R01 applications/awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute and track the percent of new competing R01 applications submitted by ESIs and percent of awards received by ESIs relative to all NIDDK R01/R37 applications and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 12 indicates the ESI share of applications declined (from ~19% in FY2011 to ~14% in FY2020) while ESI awards averaged ~22% of competing R01 awards over FY2011–FY2020, illustrating payline effects and application pool changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track mean and median ages of R01/R37 investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Report mean and median ages of investigators holding R01/R37 awards by fiscal year to monitor demographic trends and pipeline health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 13 shows small increases over time (median increased from 51 to 52 in FY2013 and then remained; mean rose ~1.2 years across decade). Use age trends alongside ESI support to infer balance of recruitment and departure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor training and career-development award counts and trends by activity code
rubrics_metrics.description: Track numbers of F (fellowship), K (career development), and T (training) awards and applications by activity code (e.g., K01, K23, K08, K99, K24) and analyze trends over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures 15A–15D document percent of budget for F/K/T awards, counts of awards, and application volumes. Note programmatic decisions (e.g., end of K24 new awards in FY2018) and trends such as growth in K23 and stability in K01/K99.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor T32 training slots and reporting lag
rubrics_metrics.description: Count the number of T32 award-associated training slots by fiscal year and note that T32 slot totals are reported at end of award period, causing reporting lag (FY2020 slots not included until later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 15E documents a decline in T32 slots from ~900 to ~750 over the decade; reporting lag caution: FY2020 T32 data may be incomplete in the report.
